title: McEwen Reports Robust Q2 Profit and Expanding Exploration Across Gold Mines
text:
McEwen posted a sharp rise in net income to $9.6 million in Q2 2026, highlighting successful exploration at Grey Fox, Tartan and Stock projects, while outlining plans to extend mine life and scale production with minimal dilution.
McEwen announced significant progress in its second quarter results and project development, highlighting a dramatic improvement in profitability and continued exploration success across its portfolio of mines.
The company reported net income of nine point six million dollars for the period ended June 30, 2026, compared with three point zero million in the same quarter of the previous year. This $9.6 million gain translates to a per share earnings figure of 0.16 dollars, up from 0.06 dollars a year earlier, a growth supported by higher gold and silver prices and improved operational efficiencies.
McEwen's management claims that the projected production stream will generate sufficient cash flow to fund further expansion while maintaining a minimal dilution profile, relying on an average gold price of four thousand dollars per ounce and a silver price of fifty dollars per ounce over the span of sixteen thousand to nineteen thousand gold equivalent units. Alongside strong financials, the company reaffirmed its All-in Sustaining Cost guidance at a range of two thousand six hundred and fifty to two thousand eight hundred and fifty dollars per gold equivalent unit, reflecting disciplined cost control.
The exploration segment underlined continued success at the Grey Fox and Tartan sites. Each operation secured new discoveries adjacent to existing underground infrastructure, reinforcing the company's capacity for organic resource expansion. At Grey Fox, the team uncovered high grade intersections within the Fox Complex, underscoring the potential to extend mine life and increase ore throughput.
Meanwhile, Tartan's drilling program has intersected the central zone over a broad area, suggesting significant upside to the mineral resource estimate for this project. McEwen also highlighted progress at the Stock mine near Timmins, a flagship project that is nearing production. The company invested twelve point eight million dollars in the Stock mine during Q2 and a total of fifty two point two million dollars since the start of last year, with development milestones reached on schedule and within budget.
The expansion of the Stock mine's life from six to eight point five years was achieved through additional engineering and mine planning, with potential further extension on the horizon. Looking forward, McEwen plans a phased approach to develop the Stock mine's increased capacity, leveraging the current milling facility to curb capital outlays.
The company is considering a larger mine and mill configuration, potentially scaling from five hundred to one thousand tonnes per day, and weighing the trade-offs between higher upfront cost and long‑term gains in production and operating efficiency. Construction of the Stock mill is set for the first half of 2027, with commercial production expected in 2027. All projects will adhere to rigorous environmental and permitting protocols, including submission of a water permit and closure plan.
Managed by a committed exploration cadre, McEwen's Q2 results reflect its disciplined approach to growth, with the company confidently forecasting continued upward momentum under the umbrella of its mining and exploration strategy
